summary: This is the backend for ShelterSim Studio, a tool for designing passive-solar winter shelters in cold high-altitude regions like Ladakh. It is a Fastify HTTP server that turns a user's shelter design (walls, roof, glazing, size, location, etc.) into a physics simulation request, runs it through the frozen @shelter/engine physics solver, and returns indoor-temperature/energy results. It also handles user accounts, lets logged-in users save designs and persist simulation runs to MongoDB, and can fetch/cache real weather data for custom (non-preset) locations from Open-Meteo or NASA POWER. It does not do any 3D rendering, UI, or the physics math itself -- those live in the client app and the @shelter/engine/@shelter/data packages respectively.

stack.name: Fastify
stack.role: The HTTP server framework: registers all routes, plugins, error handling and CORS.
stack.why: Fast, small, plugin-based -- fits a single small Node API server with schema validation built in (ajv).

stack.name: @fastify/jwt
stack.role: Signs and verifies the JWT stored in the login cookie; request.jwtVerify() is the auth check every protected route uses.
stack.why: Official Fastify plugin, integrates directly with the request/reply lifecycle and @fastify/cookie.

stack.name: @fastify/cookie
stack.role: Parses/sets the httpOnly `token` cookie that carries the JWT.
stack.why: Required by @fastify/jwt's cookie-extraction mode; avoids hand-rolling cookie parsing.

stack.name: mongoose
stack.role: ODM for MongoDB: defines the users/designs/simulations/weatherCache collections and their schemas/indexes.
stack.why: Simple schema + model API, one shared default connection reused by every model in the app.

stack.name: @shelter/engine
stack.role: The frozen physics solver: builds/validates the simulation model, runs simulate(), and formats results/errors.
stack.why: Shared, already-tested engine package -- studio-server never reimplements the physics.

stack.name: @shelter/data
stack.role: Supplies catalogue data (materials, glazings, presets, TMY weather) and weather-fetch/parse helpers (Open-Meteo/NASA POWER builders+parsers, normaliseWeather).
stack.why: Keeps material/weather science and lookups in one shared package instead of duplicated per app.

stack.name: tsx
stack.role: Runs/watches the TypeScript entry point directly (dev/start scripts) without a separate build step.
stack.why: No compile step needed for a Node ESM+TS server during development.

stack.name: vitest
stack.role: Test runner for all *.test.ts files in test/.
stack.why: Fast, Jest-like API, native ESM/TS support, shared root config for the whole monorepo.

stack.name: mongodb-memory-server
stack.role: Spins up a real, disposable MongoDB instance in-process for integration tests (auth, designs, simulations, weather cache).
stack.why: Lets tests exercise real Mongoose queries/indexes without a real MongoDB install or network.

stack.name: typescript
stack.role: Type-checks the whole package; `tsconfig.json` extends the repo's base config.
stack.why: Shared strictness/module settings across the monorepo, no per-app duplication.

layers.name: Bootstrap / env
layers.summary: src/env.ts reads process.env once into a typed Env object; src/index.ts is the real process entry point that requires MONGODB_URI/JWT_SECRET and fails fast if either is missing.

layers.name: HTTP app + error handling
layers.summary: src/app.ts builds the Fastify instance: registers cookie/JWT plugins, auth/designs/simulations/locations route plugins, CORS headers, and a single setErrorHandler that maps every known error class to its HTTP status/code (API.md §6).

layers.name: Routes
layers.summary: Each feature area (auth, designs, simulations, locations) has its own Fastify plugin file defining its routes' schemas and preHandlers, delegating all real logic to a paired service.ts.

layers.name: Services
layers.summary: Business logic called by routes: user register/login (auth/service.ts), design CRUD with ownership checks (designs/service.ts), and running+persisting a simulation (simulations/service.ts). Routes never touch Mongoose directly.

layers.name: Models
layers.summary: Mongoose schemas/models for the four MongoDB collections: users, designs, simulations, and the weatherCache. All share mongoose's one default connection set up in src/db.ts.

layers.name: Design pipeline (prepare/assemble/types/options)
layers.summary: types.ts defines the ShelterDesign contract shared with the client; assemble.ts turns a ShelterDesign into an engine SimulationRequest (materials, geometry, shape/storeys, occupancy); prepare.ts is the one entry point every route uses (it resolves custom-location weather asynchronously first, then calls assemble); options.ts builds the GET /api/options catalogue payload.

layers.name: Providers
layers.summary: A small seam (SimulationProvider interface) so routes call a named provider instead of the engine's simulate() directly; fastPhysics is the only implementation today, wrapping @shelter/engine.

layers.name: Weather
layers.summary: Resolves real weather for custom (non-preset) locations: geocoding search, Open-Meteo/NASA POWER fetch with Mongo caching, and the shared upstream-failure error type.

layers.name: Auth
layers.summary: Email+password accounts: scrypt password hashing, a Mongoose User model, a shared authenticate() preHandler guard, and register/login/logout/me routes issuing a 7-day JWT cookie.

folders.title: Auth
folders.summary: Email+password accounts: scrypt hashing (password.ts), the users Mongoose model, the shared JWT-cookie authenticate() guard, register/login logic, and the /api/auth/* routes.

folders.title: Design pipeline
folders.summary: The ShelterDesign contract type (types.ts) and the pure function (assemble.ts) that turns a ShelterDesign into an engine SimulationRequest, plus prepare.ts which adds the async custom-weather step in front of it.

folders.title: Saved designs
folders.summary: CRUD for a logged-in user's saved ShelterDesign documents: Mongoose model, ownership-checked service functions, and the /api/designs routes.

folders.title: Simulation runs
folders.summary: Runs a saved design through the physics provider and freezes the result as a persisted record (inputSnapshot + kpis + result); routes to create/list/read those runs.

folders.title: Weather
folders.summary: Everything needed to give a custom (non-catalogue) location real weather: Open-Meteo geocoding search, Open-Meteo/NASA POWER archive fetch with a Mongo-backed cache keyed by rounded lat/lon/year, and a shared UpstreamUnavailableError.

folders.title: Location search
folders.summary: A single thin route (GET /api/locations/search) that proxies to weather/geocode.ts so the client can look up coordinates for a place name.

folders.title: Providers
folders.summary: One-file seam wrapping @shelter/engine's simulate() behind a named SimulationProvider (fastPhysics), so a future alternate provider could be swapped in without route changes.

folders.title: Tests
folders.summary: Vitest integration/unit tests for the whole server: route behavior via app.inject(), real Mongo behavior via mongodb-memory-server, weather fetch/cache/geocode behavior against recorded fixtures, and a parity check against the older apps/server engine-assembly code.

models.name: User
models.fields: email (unique, lowercase, trim), name, passwordHash, createdAt

models.name: Design
models.fields: ownerId (ref User), name, design (Mixed ShelterDesign), createdAt, updatedAt

models.name: Simulation
models.fields: ownerId (ref User), designId (ref Design), provider, engineVersion, requestHash, inputSnapshot (Mixed), kpis (Mixed), weatherProvenance (Mixed, optional), result (Mixed), createdAt

models.fields: source, lat, lon, year, standardMeridian, weather (Mixed, serialised WeatherSeries)

errors.when: The ShelterDesign (or auth) request body fails its ajv schema -- bad type, out-of-range value, or unknown enum id; `field` names the offending dotted key.
location.kind==='custom' but no weatherFor hook was supplied to assemble() directly (not reachable through the routes since P3 added real resolution).
GET /api/locations/search or custom-location weather resolution: both Open-Meteo and (for weather) NASA POWER are unreachable or return a non-2xx.
The engine rejects the assembled SimulationRequest as structurally invalid.
The engine finds the building geometry inconsistent.
The engine finds the weather series invalid.
A materialId in the design isn't in @shelter/data's catalogue.
A glazingId in the design isn't in @shelter/data's catalogue.
Catalogue data doesn't match the shape the engine expects.
The engine's numerical solver failed to converge.
The engine's solve produced a singular matrix.
Request body exceeds the 5 MB limit.
Any other unexpected server error (no stack trace leaked to the client).
A protected route is called with a missing, invalid, or expired auth cookie.
POST /api/auth/register with an email already registered.
POST /api/auth/login with a wrong password or an unknown email (same message either way, to avoid leaking which).
A design or simulation id doesn't exist, or belongs to another user (ownership misses are always 404, never 403).

Real end-to-end auth + designs + simulations CRUD against a mongodb-memory-server instance.

A persisted simulation run for a custom-location design resolves and stores weatherProvenance the same way the preview route does.

A second custom-weather request for the same {source,lat,lon,year} is served from weatherCache with no network call.
GET /api/locations/search against a recorded geocoding fixture: normal results, blank query, and upstream failure.
Optional real-network smoke test against the live Open-Meteo APIs, skipped unless LIVE=1.
POST /api/simulate/preview end-to-end for a custom location, checking the returned weatherProvenance shape/notes.
resolveCustomWeather's Open-Meteo success path, its NASA POWER fallback, and its both-sources-fail error, against recorded fixtures.

env.name: PORT
env.purpose: TCP port the server listens on.

env.name: HOST
env.purpose: Network interface the server binds to.

env.name: MONGODB_URI
env.purpose: MongoDB connection string; src/index.ts exits if unset.

env.name: JWT_SECRET
env.default: undefined (required at real startup; buildApp() itself falls back to an insecure dev value for tests)
env.purpose: Secret used to sign/verify the auth JWT cookie.

env.name: NODE_ENV
env.purpose: Only 'production' makes the auth cookie Secure; also read generically by env.ts.
